lens: Pre-implementation #811 equivalence proof, simplification, and operability

findings.summary: Separate topology checks do not establish equivalence for pytest observations of internal Git state or excluded artifacts.
evidence: The contract excludes the release record and review artifact root from subject identity, binds external Git refs/merge-base, and explicitly keeps HEAD and dirtiness outside the semantic digest.
publish_release_execute.py runs quality before git add, commit, and amend. Consequently Q and P can have identical included worktree bytes while their index, HEAD, and status observations differ.

Axis-varying counterexample: a selected test reads git show HEAD:<file>, git diff --cached, or the excluded release record. Its input changes across an otherwise eligible Q-to-P transition. Checking P's parent and clean status does not prove the earlier test exercised the same input. This is a contract counterexample, not an observed failing test in the supplied files.
findings.action: Explicitly include internal Git observations and reads of excluded paths in the closure probe. Permit their normalization only after showing that pytest-release does not depend on the changed observations, or after defining and testing an equivalent observation. Otherwise fall back. Add a negative control for a selected test consuming HEAD/index or excluded record bytes; retain a positive dirty-Q-to-clean-P control so blindly hashing all Git state cannot satisfy acceptance by making reuse permanently ineligible.

findings.summary: Define pushed-object coverage precisely for the versioned reuse handoff; ancestry alone is insufficient.
evidence: The contract requires checking push-stdin objects against covered R but does not enumerate the permitted objects or tag resolution rule.
prepush_quality_receipt.py currently accepts every local object for which git merge-base --is-ancestor <object> HEAD succeeds.

Counterexample: A is an ancestor before Q's tested changes. A push containing covered R plus another ref pointing at A passes that ancestry predicate, although neither the candidate suite nor the composite establishes A's subject. Conversely, the legitimate release tag points at prepared P, as enforced by publish_release_resume.py, so requiring only raw R would reject an intended publication.
findings.action: Specify the versioned handoff's permitted pushed subjects: covered R and explicitly bound equivalent P where required by the release flow, with an explicit lightweight/annotated-tag resolution policy. Reject other ancestors unless separately verified. Add acceptance cases for R plus the legitimate P tag and R plus an unrelated older ancestor. This need not change legacy v1 behavior.

counterweight_triage.concern: Reuse only pytest-release while other gates remain current.
counterweight_triage.disposition: Coherent and appropriately narrow. The contract honestly distinguishes the measured 145.740-second pytest opportunity from the estimated remaining runtime. A general cache or reuse for every gate is unnecessary.

counterweight_triage.concern: Exact identity closure and actual savings are not yet demonstrated.
counterweight_triage.disposition: Keep these as explicit prerequisites before omitting the call. Acceptance already covers runtime, environment, external refs, materialized bytes, and subject drift; add R811-01's observational inputs. Measure hashing, sealing, current-gate mutations, and final-consumer overhead on the real eligible path.

counterweight_triage.concern: Source preservation, composite scope, and legacy handoff downgrade.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The single persistent slot, external temporary source copy, exact combined scope, and versioned reuse handoff are sufficient design choices. Add a targeted tripwire: feeding a reused composite through the v1 seal path must not produce an accepted v1 handoff. The supplied _semantic_receipt currently accepts a passing release receipt with any nonempty measured_scope; it does not distinguish reused evidence. This implements the existing versioning requirement rather than adding another receipt store.

counterweight_triage.concern: Claims-path exclusions could become a second eligibility authority.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The sole claims-validator authority, exact changed-path requirement, record binding, direct-child restriction, and rejection of non-record Q-to-P edits are coherent. Acceptance should exercise the validator's actual returned paths, including additions and prohibited replacements, without introducing another allowlist.

counterweight_triage.concern: Native changed-line reuse and publication proof.
counterweight_triage.disposition: Deferring native changed-line reuse is justified. Authorization, version checks, fresh checkout/package probes, publication, readback, and installed observations remain independently current. No additional reuse mechanism is necessary.

next_move: Amend the contract with R811-01's observational-closure rule and R811-02's pushed-object policy. Then complete the already-required bounded closure probe and positive/negative acceptance evidence before removing pytest execution. This verdict does not prevent that read-only investigation.
non_claims: Reviewed all six supplied inline semantic inputs; no workspace or provider mutation and no runtime verification.
This is a #811 pre-implementation critique, not Goal #805 resolution approval, publication approval, or a review of #810.
Requested reviewer tier metadata is not evidence that the tier was applied.
